question.worked_solution:
Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $25.$ Therefore, we can simplify the expression by factoring out $25,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}25{y}^{2}+50y+25 & = \\ 25({y}^{2}+2y+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's factor the expression inside parentheses using the square of a sum formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+2y+1 & = \\ {y}^{2}+2y+{1}^{2} & = \\ {y}^{2}+2\cdot y+{1}^{2} & = \\ (y+1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}25({y}^{2}+2y+1) & = \\ 25(y+1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
